question: Of 76 highly cited animal studies, how many were confirmed when the treatment was later tested in people?
answer: About a third: 28 of the 76. Hackam and Redelmeier found 14 more contradicted by human trials and the rest never tested in people, and these were the most cited animal papers. A mouse result is a promising lead; a headline that drops the mouse has dropped most of the doubt.
move: Ask what was studied before applying a finding to people.
ask: When I read a hopeful health headline, do I check whether it was tested in people like me?
trap: About nine in ten, since these were the most respected studies.
reference: Hackam & Redelmeier, Translation of research evidence from animals to humans, JAMA 296:1731–1732, 2006
